issues.legal_issue: A planning designation permitting commercial use does not by itself alter a lease that restricts the land to residential use.
material_facts: The land was leased for residential use, and a residential building stood on it.
A later planning document designated the area for commercial use.
The lessees sought to change the land’s use under the lease.
issues.conclusion: The planning designation was enabling only; it did not automatically or statutorily convert the land’s use or authorize the lessees to change use unilaterally contrary to the lease.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 7 of the Delhi Development Act, 1957, the Master Plan could remove planning restrictions on commercial use, but it did not displace the lease agreement. A change of use contrary to the agreement required the parties’ agreement; no earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.lease_user_conversion_dispute: The dispute concerns a lessee seeking to change the use of leased land.
predicates.lease_restricts_user_change_without_less: The lease limits the land to a particular use unless the lessor agrees to a change.
predicates.master_plan_designated_commercial_use: A planning document permits commercial use in the area containing the leased land.

issues.definition: When a lessee seeks a different use of leased land, a planning designation permitting that use does not itself change a lease that requires the lessor’s agreement.

issues.legal_issue: A request to change the use of leased land is not a valid conversion application merely because it asks about the terms and charges for the change.
material_facts: An earlier letter asked the authority to state the terms and charges for constructing a commercial building.
That letter was not signed by all the co-lessees and did not request permission to change the land’s use or show willingness to comply with the conditions.
After the authority asked for a fresh application signed by all co-lessees, a later application in the prescribed form was submitted with their signatures.
issues.conclusion: The earlier letter was only an enquiry, not an application for conversion. The first duly made application was the later application signed by all co-lessees; the absence of a prescribed form at the time of the earlier letter did not make that enquiry an application.
issues.legal_principle: A conversion application must at least request permission to change the land’s use on behalf of all lessees and show readiness and willingness to comply with the conditions. An enquiry about terms and charges is insufficient, whether or not a prescribed form was then available. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.lease_user_conversion_dispute: The dispute concerns a lessee seeking permission to change the use of leased land.
predicates.earlier_communication_only_sought_terms: The lessees’ earlier communication asked what conditions or charges would apply rather than requesting permission to change the land’s use.
predicates.earlier_communication_not_signed_by_all_: The earlier communication was not signed by all lessees or by someone shown to be authorized to act for all of them.
predicates.later_conversion_request_signed_by_all_l: The lessees later submitted a request to change the land’s use that was signed by all of them.

issues.definition: Where the earlier communication only enquires about terms and is not signed by all lessees, a later conversion request signed by all lessees is the first valid application.

issues.legal_issue: Conversion charges are calculated by reference to the date of the valid application when the authority’s later processing delay is not attributable to the applicants.
material_facts: The first valid application was submitted by all co-lessees on February 27, 1981.
The authority granted permission on January 12, 1984, and the record contained no explanation for the delay in responding to the application.
The authority had calculated the additional premium using a later date based on an assumed processing period.
issues.conclusion: The additional premium had to be calculated using the rate prevalent on the date of the valid application, February 27, 1981.
issues.legal_principle: Conversion charges are reckoned from the date of the valid application. An authority should process an application as early as possible and cannot use the end of an assumed processing period as the charge date without valid reasons or delay attributable to the applicants. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.lease_user_conversion_dispute: The dispute concerns a lessee seeking permission to change the use of leased land.
predicates.valid_conversion_application_submitted: The lessees submitted a request that satisfied the requirements for a conversion application.
predicates.authority_delay_not_attributable_to_appl: The authority did not explain its delay in responding, and the delay was not shown to have been caused by the applicants.

issues.definition: When a valid conversion application is submitted and the authority’s delay is not attributable to the applicants, conversion charges are calculated from the application date.

issues.legal_issue: Interest on an additional premium is chargeable only after the lessees’ permitted time to pay following notice has expired.
material_facts: The authority notified the lessees of the additional premium on January 12, 1984.
The lessees were allowed three months from that notice to make payment.
The Court directed that interest be charged from April 12, 1984.
issues.conclusion: Interest on the additional premium was chargeable from the end of the three-month payment period after notice, namely April 12, 1984.
issues.legal_principle: Where the authority allows a period after notice for payment of an additional premium, interest is chargeable after that period expires. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.lease_user_conversion_dispute: The dispute concerns a lessee seeking permission to change the use of leased land.
predicates.additional_premium_notified: The authority notified the lessees that an additional premium was payable for conversion.
predicates.lessees_given_payment_grace_after_notice: The lessees were allowed time after receiving notice to pay the additional premium.

issues.definition: When an additional premium is notified and the lessees are given time to pay, interest begins after that payment period expires.

issues.legal_issue: Misuse charges remain payable until conversion charges begin to apply.
material_facts: The lessees were liable for misuse charges while the land was being used contrary to its existing permitted use.
Conversion charges became payable from April 12, 1984.
The authority’s notice listed the relevant misuse charges.
issues.conclusion: The lessees were liable for the specified misuse charges up to April 12, 1984, from which date conversion charges applied.
issues.legal_principle: Misuse charges are payable for the period of misuse before conversion charges begin; the Court relied on the terms of the authority’s notice and the circumstances of the conversion. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.lease_user_conversion_dispute: The dispute concerns a lessee seeking permission to change the use of leased land.
predicates.land_used_in_misuse_before_conversion_ch: The lessees used the land contrary to its permitted use before conversion charges began to apply.

issues.definition: When leased land is misused before conversion charges begin, misuse charges are payable until conversion charges begin.

issues.legal_issue: A lessee may not put a changed use into effect until the additional premium and interest have been paid in full, although payment may be permitted by instalments.
material_facts: The authority offered permission to convert the land’s use subject to payment of an additional premium and interest.
The Court allowed the additional premium to be paid in three equal annual instalments, with interest on the deferred payment at no more than 14 per cent per annum.
The Court directed that the lessees could not convert the land’s use until the last instalment and its interest were paid.
The Court also allowed other amounts, apart from conversion charges, to be paid in monthly instalments with interest at no more than 10 per cent per annum.
issues.conclusion: The lessees could not convert the land to commercial use until the entire additional premium and interest were paid. The additional premium could be paid in three equal annual instalments with interest at no more than 14 per cent per annum, and the other amounts could be paid in 24 monthly instalments with interest at no more than 10 per cent per annum.
issues.legal_principle: Where permission to change the leased use is conditional on payment of an additional premium, the changed use cannot take effect before that premium and applicable interest are fully paid. In the circumstances, the Court directed instalment facilities and capped interest on deferred payments. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.lease_user_conversion_dispute: The dispute concerns a lessee seeking permission to change the use of leased land.
predicates.conversion_permission_conditional_on_add: The authority made permission to change the land’s use conditional on payment of an additional premium.

issues.definition: When permission to change leased land’s use is conditional on an additional premium, the changed use cannot take effect until the premium and interest are fully paid.
